        <p class="eil3-eyebrow">01 / The decision</p>
        <h1 id="eil3-title">Same grades, <em>different futures?</em></h1>
        <p class="eil3-deck">Getting into university is a major decision. <strong>But it isn't the last.</strong></p>
        <p class="eil3-prose">Students enter university with expectations about their chances of success. By the end of the first year, they have something they did not have before: <strong>information about how well they are doing.</strong></p>
        <div class="eil3-path" aria-label="Theoretical sequence: university entry, first-year results and reassessment, then another educational decision">
          <div class="eil3-path-first"><span class="eil3-path-num">01 / ENTRY</span><strong>Enter university</strong><small>Expectations about success</small></div>

          <span class="eil3-path-arrow" aria-hidden="true">→</span>
          <div class="eil3-path-first eil3-path-last"><span class="eil3-path-num">03 / WHAT NEXT?</span><strong>A new decision</strong><small>What educational options now seem possible?</small></div>
        </div>
        <p class="eil3-turn">When first-year results are disappointing, <strong>do the routes students take differ by family background?</strong></p>
        <div class="eil3-screen-actions"><button class="eil3-button" type="button" data-go="1">Let's explore <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></button></div>

        <h2 id="eil3-figure-title">When things go well, <em>the gap is small.</em></h2>
        <p class="eil3-prose" id="eil3-figure-deck">Let's compare students with different family backgrounds who passed <strong>80% of their first-year credits.</strong> Most remain in the same degree, and dropout is low in both groups.</p>

      <section class="eil3-screen" data-screen="2" aria-labelledby="eil3-meaning-title" hidden>
        <p class="eil3-eyebrow">03 / What it means</p>
        <h2 id="eil3-meaning-title">The same setback. <em>Different ways forward.</em></h2>
        <p class="eil3-deck">Academic results are new information. But students may not have the same resources to respond to them.</p>
        <p class="eil3-prose">When a first year goes badly, students may rethink whether the degree is right for them, whether another route is available or whether continuing is feasible. This is where <strong>compensatory advantage</strong> offers a sociological interpretation.</p>
        <div class="eil3-ideas" aria-label="Possible mechanisms for socially differentiated educational decisions">
          <div><span>Expectations</span><strong>“Can I still succeed?”</strong><p>Results may prompt students to reassess their chances of completing the degree.</p></div>
          <div><span>Information</span><strong>“What other routes exist?”</strong><p>Knowledge of alternatives and familiarity with the university system can differ.</p></div>
          <div><span>Resources</span><strong>“Can I afford to try again?”</strong><p>Support and the costs of changing direction can make options more or less feasible.</p></div>
        </div>
        <p class="eil3-interpret-note">These are <strong>plausible explanatory mechanisms</strong>, not resources measured as the direct causes of each student's decision in the study.</p>
        <div class="eil3-seventy"><strong>When do these inequalities fade?</strong> As performance improves, differences in predicted dropout narrow. Around <strong>70% of credits passed</strong>, the study no longer detects statistically significant gaps in dropout — not an exact threshold, and not proof that all pathways become identical.</div>
        <div class="eil3-screen-actions eil3-screen-actions-spread"><button class="eil3-text-button" type="button" data-go="1">← Back to the evidence</button><button class="eil3-button" type="button" data-go="3">See the sociological discovery <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></button></div>
      </section>

      <section class="eil3-screen eil3-outro" data-screen="3" aria-labelledby="eil3-conclusion-title" hidden>
        <p class="eil3-eyebrow">04 / Your sociological insight</p>
        <h2 id="eil3-conclusion-title">Inequality doesn't end <em>at the university gate.</em></h2>
        <div class="eil3-insight-card">
          <p class="eil3-eyebrow">The discovery</p>
          <h3>When academic results are good, social differences in dropout are small. <em>When things go wrong, different ways forward emerge.</em></h3>
          <p>Getting into university is one socially structured transition. Decisions made after the first year can be another. New evidence about academic performance meets the expectations, information and resources students bring with them.</p>
        </div>
        <p class="eil3-final-line">Educational inequality is not only about <em>who gets in.</em> It is also about <strong>what becomes possible after a setback.</strong></p>

Outcomes refer to progression after the first year, not eventual graduation.</p></div>
